en_excerpt: Jewel and I come up from the field, following the path in single file.
fa_excerpt: من و جوئل داریم از سر زمین برمی‌گردیم، من از جلو او از عقب.
analysis: The participial phrase is not imitated. Daryabandari converts the visual relation into an independent Persian clause. The event is preserved while English grammatical packaging is discarded.
rule: Reconstruct the scene or relation first; then choose the Persian syntax that makes that relation immediately intelligible.
academic_transfer: Useful for compressed academic participial phrases: unpack the relation when literal compression produces translationese.

en_excerpt: The cakes turned out right well.
fa_excerpt: کیک‌ها خیلی خوب از آب درآمدند.
analysis: A literal equivalent of 'turned out' is avoided. The native Persian resultative idiom از آب درآمدن carries the same everyday evaluative force. Cora's repeated concern with the cakes is kept rather than stylistically cleaned up.
rule: Prefer an established Persian construction that performs the same discourse function over a lexical calque.
academic_transfer: For evaluative or resultative academic phrases, search for established Persian collocations before reproducing English verb structure.

en_excerpt: Warmish-cool, with a faint taste like the hot July wind in cedar trees smells.
fa_excerpt: آب نیمه‌خنک مزهٔ ملایمی داره، مثل بوی بادی که وسط تابستون از لای درخت‌های کاج بیاد.
analysis: The synesthetic oddity is retained: taste remains compared with smell. Daryabandari makes the relation grammatically Persian without explaining the image away.
rule: When an image is strange because the author intends it to be strange, naturalize the grammar—not the image.
academic_transfer: Preserve conceptual metaphors and unusual comparisons in theory/history writing, while allowing Persian syntax to carry them.

en_excerpt: Where she's got to see him. Where every breath she draws is full of his knocking and sawing...
fa_excerpt: درست زیر چشم آدی... هر نفسی که آدی می‌کشه پر از صدای اره و چکش اوست.
analysis: The English fragments are not reproduced mechanically. Their pressure and accusatory rhythm are rebuilt through short Persian units, colloquial syntax, repetition, and forceful verbs.
rule: Preserve the rhetorical pressure of fragmentation even when individual fragment boundaries must change.
academic_transfer: In polemical or emphatic prose, preserve argumentative rhythm and repetition, but do not force English fragment syntax onto Persian.

en_excerpt: if the sack is full, I cannot help it.
fa_excerpt: ولی اگه توبره‌ام پر شد دیگه دست خودم نیست.
analysis: The literal phrase 'I cannot help it' becomes the idiomatic Persian دست خودم نیست. More importantly, Daryabandari preserves Dewey Dell's circular self-justification rather than rationalizing it.
rule: Translate the speaker's cognitive pattern, not merely the propositions.
academic_transfer: When an author deliberately circles, qualifies, or repeats an argument, do not edit away the reasoning pattern merely to make Persian cleaner.

en_excerpt: I done holp him so much already I cant quit now.
fa_excerpt: این‌قد بهش کمک کرده‌ام که حالا دیگه نمی‌تونم نکنم.
analysis: Daryabandari does not imitate English grammatical error. He gives Tull a plausible Persian oral sentence whose slightly recursive structure carries the same rustic, matter-of-fact personality.
rule: Do not reproduce source-language ungrammaticality mechanically; reproduce the social and expressive value it creates.
academic_transfer: For academic prose this becomes: translate marked register as marked Persian register, not as grammatical damage.

en_excerpt: when He aims for something to stay put, He makes it up-and-down ways, like a tree or a man.
fa_excerpt: اگه بخواد یک چیزی سر جاش وایسه سرپا درستش می‌کنه، مثل درخت یا آدم.
analysis: The English opposition longways/up-and-down is rebuilt with Persian embodied expressions such as درازش می‌کنه and سرپا درستش می‌کنه. The absurd folk theology remains intact, but the wording sounds generated inside Persian.
rule: Find the Persian conceptual opposition that lets the same reasoning work, rather than preserving the source's grammatical labels.
academic_transfer: Excellent model for conceptual prose: preserve the relation or opposition, but recode it in Persian's own conceptual and syntactic resources.

en_excerpt: I believed death to be a phenomenon of the body; now I know it to be merely a function of the mind.
fa_excerpt: خیال می‌کردم مرگ پدیده‌ای است مربوط به بدن آدم؛ حالا می‌فهمم که فقط یکی از احوال روحی آدمه.
analysis: The translation rises from colloquial narration into conceptual Persian without becoming a word-for-word philosophical calque. 'function of the mind' is rendered as one of the states/conditions of mind, preserving the thought while choosing more idiomatic Persian abstraction.
rule: Register is local. A translator may move between colloquial and conceptual Persian inside one voice when the source does.
academic_transfer: Directly relevant to Zero Hour: use natural Persian conceptual prose, not English-derived noun chains.

en_excerpt: It was not her. I was there, looking. I saw.
fa_excerpt: خودش نبود. من اونجا بودم. نگاه کردم. دیدم.
analysis: Daryabandari resists the temptation to clarify the child's broken logic. Short clauses remain short; pronoun instability and repetitive perception remain part of the experience.
rule: Ambiguity and cognitive distortion can be meaning-bearing; do not repair them unless Persian grammar makes comprehension impossible.
academic_transfer: For difficult theoretical prose, distinguish genuine source ambiguity from accidental awkwardness before 'clarifying' it.

en_excerpt: I made it on the bevel.
analysis: Instead of explaining 'bevel' generically, Daryabandari activates an existing Persian carpentry term: فارسی کردن / فارسی‌بُر. The numbered procedural structure is preserved.
rule: Before inventing a descriptive equivalent, ask whether the target language already has a domain-native operation or term.
academic_transfer: For humanities terminology, consult established Persian disciplinary usage before creating calques; keep the project glossary separate from dictionary evidence.

en_excerpt: words are no good; ... words dont ever fit even what they are trying to say at.
fa_excerpt: کلمات هیچ به درد نمی‌خورند؛ ... کلمات حتی با همون مطلبی هم که می‌خوان بگن جور درنمی‌آن.
analysis: The abstract claim is made Persian through به درد خوردن and جور درآمدن rather than formal lexical symmetry. Yet the philosophical distinction between word and lived experience remains intact.
rule: Abstract thought does not require abstract-sounding Persian. Use ordinary Persian verbs when they express the conceptual relation more exactly.
academic_transfer: Core rule for Zero Hour: prefer precise Persian verbal relations over inflated nominal prose.

en_excerpt: I knelt and confessed to God and asked for guidance and received it.
fa_excerpt: زانو زدم در پیشگاه خداوند اعتراف کردم؛ التماس ارشاد کردم و ارشاد شدم.
analysis: Daryabandari sharply changes register for Whitfield. Instead of ordinary colloquial Persian, he activates elevated religious Persian—پیشگاه، ارشاد، بخشایش، ظلّ محبت لایزال—matching the preacher's self-dramatizing biblical rhetoric.
rule: Translate register with a target-language register system, not with the same vocabulary used for every narrator.
academic_transfer: Different source authors and quoted voices in Zero Hour should not all sound alike; preserve disciplinary, historical, and rhetorical register distinctions.
